source.title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit

accepted.question_text: What is the relation, if any, between stellar mass and the convective core overshooting parameter β that measures the extent of extra mixing beyond the formal convective-core boundary in stellar evolution models? In particular, can a physically meaningful mass–β relation be established, or do different analyses of binary-star systems support incompatible values of β even when the stellar masses are well measured?

evidence.quote: Many authors have attempted to determine the exact relation, if any, between the stellar mass and the value of the convective core overshooting parameter, with opposing findings

accepted.question_text: For the detached eclipsing binary system Ai Phe, whose primary star has already undergone first dredge-up while the secondary has not, how robust are stellar-model calibrations—especially the inferred system age and the convective core overshooting parameter β—to assumptions about microscopic diffusion and surface metallicity evolution? More specifically, if microscopic diffusion is allowed to alter the observable surface [Fe/H] of the stars versus being effectively canceled at the surface by competing mixing processes, do the same precise masses, radii, temperatures, and metallicity measurements lead to materially different calibrations?

evidence.quote: Aims. Relying on recently available and very precise observational data for the Ai Phe binary system, we explore the robustness of the calibration of stellar models achievable with this system.

a firm prediction of the surface metallicity for stars in the mass range of Ai Phe before the first dredge-up is problematic. This poses an interesting question as to the robustness of the fit obtained for similar systems

The comparison of the calibrations obtained under the two scenarios allows us to investigate their robustness to different choices of the efficiency of the microscopic diffusion in this critical mass range.

accepted.question_text: When fitting stellar models to a precisely observed binary system such as Ai Phe, do different stellar codes, inference pipelines, or modelling assumptions about microscopic diffusion and other extra-mixing processes produce different estimates of the system age and convective core overshooting efficiency? If they do, to what extent are the inferred calibration parameters properties of the stars themselves rather than artifacts of the modeller's chosen input physics and estimation pipeline?

evidence.quote: Different stellar codes, relying on different assumptions about the microscopic diffusion efficiency, and given the inclusion of extra-mixing mechanisms, may obtain different age and/or overshooting efficiency calibrations on the same target system.
It is well known that different pipelines, adopting different estimation algorithms and different stellar tracks, might obtain different estimates of the system fundamental parameters
great care should be taken when adopting binary systems for parameter calibrations, because the obtained parameters may only reflect the decisions by the modellers in their stellar model computations

accepted.question_text: Can binary systems in the approximately 1.2–1.5 M⊙ mass range be used to robustly constrain free parameters in stellar evolution calculations, or are the resulting calibrations too sensitive to uncertain surface-[Fe/H] evolution and related modelling choices? In the specific case of Ai Phe, which of the competing surface-metallicity scenarios is the more reliable description of the system, and can precise measurements of the individual stellar surface [Fe/H] values discriminate between those scenarios?

evidence.quote: As such this investigation raises some doubt as to the robustness of the calibrations obtained in the mass range between 1.2 M⊙ and 1.5 M⊙.
every system provides different challenges and poses interesting questions about the possibility to use them to constrain free parameters in stellar model computations.
In this specific case, precise measurements of individual surface [Fe/H] would be of utmost importance in helping us to judge which scenario is the most reliable.
